prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a mortgage application waiting on payslips. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a case is waiting on payslips, I should check whether the latest payroll date has already passed and whether the member has a realistic chance regularity."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I am chasing payslips, I prefer to ask for them in a single clear request with the exact date range needed, because multiple small asks tend to slow the case and confuse the member."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member says payslips are delayed due to a changed payday or a new employer, I should expect a one-off gap and look for arrive."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the pay pattern varies because of overtime, commission or shift allowances, I need a wider look back across payslips instead of relying on one month,
